speaker: Teacher (charter: proof for the deluded)
question: What initiation is taught, and for whom?
premises: atha dīkṣāṃ bruve — Now I speak initiation: authorial first person opens the proof-arc.
mūḍhajanāśvāsapradāyinīm — giving confidence to the deluded (mūḍha = under Māyā's sway): the rite answers doubt, not attainment.
inference: Charter: a dīkṣā whose fruit is confidence itself, for those still under delusion.

speaker: Teacher (the fire-seat imagined)
question: What is visualized, and where?
premises: trikoṇe vahnisadane — in the triangle, the fire's seat: the imagined altar.
vahnivarṇojjvale 'bhitaḥ vāyavyapuranirdhūte — blazing all around with the fire-letter, fanned by the wind-abode: two elements stoke it.
kare savye sujājvale — on the left hand, fiercely blazing (savya = left; secondary 'right' noted as slip).
inference: The imagined apparatus: triangle fire-seat on the left palm, letter-fueled, wind-fanned.

speaker: Teacher (the burning visualized)
question: What is done with the seed?
premises: bījaṃ kiṃcid gṛhītvā — having taken a little seed: the demonstration needs almost nothing.
etat tathaiva hṛdayāntare kare ca dahyamānaṃ — this very seed burning both in the hand and likewise inside the heart: outer and inner fires one act.
sat cintayet tajjapaikayuk — let the true one visualize, absorbed solely in its muttering: truth of the visualizer conditions the proof.
inference: The visualization: a little seed burned in hand and heart together by the muttering-absorbed true one.

speaker: Teacher (seedlessness)
question: What happens to the burned seed?
premises: vahnidīpitaphaṭkāradhoraṇīdāhapīḍitam — oppressed by the burning of the fire-kindled unbroken phaṭ-series: the mantra-weapon named.
bījaṃ nirbījatāmeti — the seed goes to seedlessness: sterility as the demonstrated state.
svasūtikaraṇākṣamam — unable to produce its own fruit: the definition of what burning proves.
inference: The demonstration's core: mantra-fire renders the seed incapable of fruit — sterility made visible.

speaker: Teacher (from seed to mala)
question: How does the seed-demo transfer to the soul?
premises: taptaṃ na etat prarohāya — roasted, this is not for sprouting: the seed-side stated flat.
tenaiva pratyayena tu — yet by that very proof: the transfer-word.
malamāyākhyakarmāṇi mantradhyānakriyābalāt — the karmas called mala and māyā, by mantra-meditation-rite force, [are burned] (verb carried to v6).
inference: The transfer announced: as with seed, so with mala — by the same threefold force.

speaker: Teacher (Śambhunātha's demo)
question: Who showed this, and to what end?
premises: dagdhāni na svakāryāya — burned up, not for their effect: the karmas' sterility (completing v5).
nirbījapratyayaṃ tu imam — but this seedlessness-proof: singled out as the teaching's jewel.
sa śrīmān suprasanno me śambhunātho nyarūpayat — the venerable, most gracious Śambhunātha demonstrated it to me: Kulaguru credited, grace noted.
inference: The lineage seal on the proof: received from gracious Śambhunātha, not invented.

speaker: Teacher (the seed's joining)
question: What more is done with the seed, and why does it work so widely?
premises: bījasyāpi atra kāryā ca yojanā — of the seed too the joining is to be done here: the burned seed is still joined (to the Supreme).
kṛpayā guroḥ — by the guru's grace: joining is gift, not technique.
yato dīkṣā sudīptatvāt sthāvarāṇyapi mocayet — since initiation by brilliance liberates even the immobile: the proof's range covers plants and minerals.
inference: The joining completes the burning; brilliance explains the boundless range.

speaker: Teacher (who may give proof)
question: Whose initiation carries visible proof?
premises: yo guruḥ japahomārcādhyānasiddhatvam ātmani jñātvā — the guru who, having known in himself mastery of muttering, fire-offering, worship, meditation.
dīkṣāṃ caret — performs initiation: the condition met, the act follows.
tasya dīkṣā sapratyayā smṛtā — his initiation is held proof-bearing: siddhatva in, pratyaya out.
inference: The competence law: only self-known mastery in the four yields proof-bearing initiation.

speaker: Teacher (who is exempt)
question: For whom is this rule not?
premises: avadhūte nirācāre tattvajñe na tu ayaṃ vidhiḥ — not for the shaken-off, the conductless, the tattva-knower is this rule: three exemptions.
sācāraiḥ kriyate dīkṣā — by the conduct-bound is initiation performed: the rule's true addressee.
yā dṛṣṭapratyayānvitā — which is endowed with seen proof: the proof belongs to the bound, not the free.
inference: Exemption map: the free need no proof; the bound receive it through rite.
uncertainties: nirācāra per Jayaratha = the knower (lore); sācāra = for whom rite is essential.

speaker: Teacher (knowledge self-proved)
question: Why does the conductless one need no proof?
premises: nirācāreṇa dīkṣāyāṃ pratyayaḥ tu na gadyate — by the conductless one no proof is declared in initiation.
jñānaṃ svapratyayaṃ — knowledge is its own proof: the axiom.
yasmāt na phalāntaram arhati — since it deserves no further fruit: self-proved needs no sequel.
inference: The axiom: knowledge proves itself, so no rite need prove it.

speaker: Teacher (the balance test)
question: What proof joins the sācāra practice?
premises: dhyānādi tu phalāt sādhyam iti siddhāmatoditam — 'through the fruit, meditation and the rest are effected,' thus the Siddhāmata teaches (compression flagged).
tulāśuddhiparīkṣāṃ vā kuryāt — or let him perform the balance-purity test: the named alternative.
pratyayayoginīm — the proof-joining [test]:joinedness is the test's essence.
inference: Two proof-yogas for the bound: fruit-effected practice (Siddhāmata) or the balance test.
uncertainties: phalāt sādhyam compression — best reading flagged.

speaker: Teacher (canon list)
question: Where is the balance test recorded?
premises: yathā śrītantrasadbhāve kathitā parameśinā — as told in the Tantrasadbhāva by the Supreme Lord.
śrīpūrvaśāstre api eṣā ca sūcitā parameśinā — and in the Pūrvaśāstra too this is indicated by the Supreme Lord (Mālinīvijaya, lore).
Double divine attestation: told and indicated, both by the Lord.
inference: Canon seal: the test is twice divinely attested.

speaker: Teacher (the five signs)
question: What are śakti's grades?
premises: ānanda udbhavaḥ kampaḥ nidrā ghūrṇī ca pañcamī — bliss, uprising, tremor, sleep, and whirling the fifth: the five fears decoded as śakti-signs.
iti evam vadatā — 'thus' by him who says (the Pūrvaśāstra's voice).
śaktitāratamyābhidhāyinā — by the teacher of śakti's gradation: the list grades śaktipāta itself.
inference: The five signs read as śakti's ladder, not pathology.

speaker: Teacher (levitation mechanism)
question: How does uprising work?
premises: udbhavaḥ laghubhāvena — the uprising comes through lightness: the means.
dehagrahatirohiteḥ — from concealment of body-grasp (ablative cause; genitive considered): the condition.
dehaḥ hi pārthivaḥ mukhyaḥ tadā mukhyatvam ujjhati — for the body is earthen and chief — then it abandons chiefness: matter demoted when grasp conceals it.
inference: Mechanism: lightness lifts when body-grasp hides; the earthen chief is demoted.
uncertainties: dehagrahatirohiteḥ case: ablative hetu chosen; genitive considered — convergent.

speaker: Teacher (the levitation rite)
question: How is the test performed?
premises: bhāvilāghavamantreṇa — with the forthcoming-levitation mantra: the instrument.
śiṣyaṃ dhyātvā samutplutam — having meditated the disciple floated up: visualization precedes weighing.
karmāṇi tatra aśeṣāṇi pūrvoktāni ācaret guruḥ — let the guru perform there all remaining rites as before stated: the test nests inside the full rite.
inference: Procedure: levitation-mantra, visualized floating, then the remaining rites as usual.

speaker: Lineage seal
question: What has been taught?
premises: uktā sā iyam — told is this very [rite]: perfective seal.
tulāśuddhidīkṣā — the balance-purity initiation: named whole.
pratyayadāyinī — the giver of proof: its essence as its epithet.
inference: Colophon: the proof-giving balance initiation stands taught.
